ideas.question: What is the association between maternal weight gain patterns during pregnancy (measured in PRAMS Phase 8) and SUID incidence in infants from CDC linked birth/infant death data?
ideas.why_open: The existing studies have not examined the specific trajectory of maternal weight gain throughout pregnancy as a risk factor for SUID. Understanding this relationship could provide insights into interventions targeting gestational weight management.
ideas.data: Maternal Weight and Care, Birth Location and Time

ideas.question: How does maternal exposure to different environmental factors (recorded in NFR-CRS) affect SUID incidence across various geographic locations using CDC natality data?
ideas.why_open: Environmental exposures have not been thoroughly investigated for their role in SUID. Analyzing these exposures from the detailed NFR-CRS records can uncover regional disparities and new risk factors.

ideas.question: How do socioeconomic status indicators (from PRAMS Phase 7) correlate with SUID incidence in infants from the CDC linked birth/infant death data?
ideas.why_open: Socioeconomic determinants of health have not been fully explored as contributors to SUID. Identifying these correlations can help target public health interventions.

ideas.question: What is the impact of maternal prenatal care quality (from PRAMS Phase 8) on SUID rates in infants from CDC natality and linked death data?
ideas.why_open: The effect of varying levels of prenatal care quality has not been well-studied with respect to SUID. This could provide insights into how improving prenatal services can reduce risk.
ideas.data: Healthcare Visits During Pregnancy, Medical Conditions

ideas.question: Can maternal postpartum mental health status (recorded in PRAMS Phase 7) predict SUID risk in infants from the CDC linked birth/infant death data?
ideas.why_open: Postpartum mental health has not been extensively examined as a predictor for SUID. This research could highlight new areas of intervention focusing on maternal mental wellness.
ideas.data: Postpartum Mental Health, Demographics and Dates
